BRICKS USED BY THE ATLAS: VECTORS (November 2026)
==============================================================================================================
Every brick (atom, template, shifted template) with its vector. 'OURS' = found by us and not present in the tables of bounds used by the Atlas (Radziszowski's survey rev. 18, Rowley). It does NOT mean that
the brick is new: for most of our atoms the size is at most the published bound for the same parameters, so a colouring of that size (possibly non-linear or circulant) may already be known. Priority has not been checked.

HOW TO READ THE VECTORS
  ATOM (linear colouring of N vertices 0..N-1): N-1 digits; digit d (d = 1..N-1) is the colour of the LENGTH d: the edge {i,j} has the colour of the digit |i-j|.
      Colours 0, 1, 2, ... are numbered in INCREASING ORDER OF THE LIMITS: for (3,4,5) colour 0 has no K3, colour 1 no K4, colour 2 no K5. An atom with limits (k1..kr) on N vertices proves R(k1..kr) >= N + 1.
      Circulant atoms are written in full: length d and length N-d have the same colour.
  TEMPLATE (Rowley): a period of m-1 digits; digits 0, 1, ... are the template colours, J = JOKER (a triangle-free length reserved for a colour of the base); phi = number of lengths before the first J.
      Composition with an atom V of n vertices: for mu = 1..n-1 write the period, each J replaced by the colour of length mu of V; then append the first phi digits of the period. Result: N = (m-1)(n-1) + 1 + phi vertices.
  SHIFTED TEMPLATE (kA <= kB added colours, width q, tail t): one vector of 3q + t digits = row F (q digits, alpha = 1), row M (q digits, alpha = 2..p-1), row L (q digits, alpha = p), then the tail (t digits).
      0 = first added colour; 1 = second added colour; J = colour of the base at length alpha; 2 = colour of the base at length alpha-1 (shift); 3 = colour of the base at length alpha+1 (not used here).
